newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stoiber says German history demands a stable euro.
newsitem.headline: Stoiber says German history demands a stable euro.

text.p: Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber reaffirmed on Wednesday his call for a strict reading of entry criteria for the monetary union, saying that German history made it critical to have a stable currency.
Stoiber said in the text of a speech to a Bundesbank reception ahead of a council meeting on Thursday that social peace in Germany could be endangered if the new euro were not as stable as the mark.

"After the horrible experience of Germany with inflation and currency reform, a stable currency is a basic value that cannot be put into play because that could endanger social peace in our land," Stoiber said.
"That's why we have always explained that the new European currency must be as stable as the mark. That is what we promised in signing the Maastricht Treaty and that is what we must do," he said.
Stoiber said it was important for the European Union to develop common finance, budget and economic policies to secure the stability of the euro.

In the absence of such policies, a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty, which contains guidelines for membership in the new currency set to begin in January 1999, should be followed, he said.
"A stable euro, I repeat a stable euro, is a major chance for the German and European economies," he said.
